newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malakoff eyes more overseas power plants.
newsitem.headline: Malakoff eyes more overseas power plants.

text.p: Malaysian power firm Malakoff Bhd said on Tuesday it was in talks to build electricity generation plants in India and Ghana as part of its overseas expansion plans.
Malakoff managing director Ahmad Jauhari Yahya told reporters after the company's annual meeting that the company was also interested in power project ventures in neighbouring countries.
In India, the planned greenfield project would be carried out in partnership with an Indian firm. He did not give any other details.
He said the company have also started preliminary discussions on a power plant project in Ghana, but also did not provide details.
"We are very serious" about venturing abroad, Ahmad said, stressing that Malakoff will maintain the energy business as its core activity.

Malakoff earlier this month said it was seeking a 60 percent stake in a 120 megawatt hydropower project in Bosnia. The company is also diversifying into steel and iron manufacture with a 40 percent stake in a steel mill in Bosnia.
